title: Già hóa dân số và tuổi nghỉ hưu · Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some societies are considering raising the retirement age as life expectancy increases. What problems could this create, and what measures could be taken to address them?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

grammar.why: Trong câu mở, but nối lợi ích dự kiến với giới hạn thực hiện cụ thể. Mở bài nêu đúng mối nối tài chính giữa tuổi thọ và hưu trí, đồng thời tách khả năng làm việc của cá nhân khỏi chỉ số trung bình để tránh suy luận từ dân số sang mọi nghề.

paragraphs: Longer lives increase pension costs, but the ability to work longer depends on health and occupation rather than the national average lifespan alone. A uniform increase can force unhealthy workers to remain in strenuous jobs; occupation-based eligibility and gradual retirement can prevent pension savings from being achieved through disproportionate harm to those least able to continue.

Healthy life expectancy and physical demands differ sharply between occupations. Longer average lives can conceal large differences in years of good health. Requiring physically demanding work to continue on the same terms as desk-based employment may shift pension savings onto people least able to extend their working lives safely. An increase in average life expectancy does not mean that a construction worker and an office adviser can safely extend their careers by the same number of years.

Eligibility for earlier pensions should reflect documented occupational demands, while part-time transitions let healthier employees reduce workloads without losing their entire earned income at once. Retirement rules should allow earlier exit for demanding work and gradual retirement for others. Earlier access for demanding occupations needs clear eligibility, while gradual retirement should remain a practical option rather than depend entirely on individual employers' goodwill. A construction worker with documented physical limitations should not have to demonstrate the same remaining work capacity as an adviser who can reduce hours and perform lighter duties. Clear eligibility rules also make earlier access predictable for workers planning their exit, while preventing an occupational exception from becoming an arbitrary favour granted by individual managers. Pension reform should balance contribution periods with healthy life expectancy and occupational demands, rather than use longevity alone to justify a uniform retirement age.
Pension sustainability requires longer contributions from those who can manage them, together with protection for workers whose health makes an equally long career unrealistic.

paragraphs.quote: Eligibility for earlier pensions should reflect documented occupational demands, while part-time transitions let healthier employees reduce workloads without losing their entire earned income at once. Retirement rules should allow earlier exit for demanding work and gradual retirement for others. Earlier access for demanding occupations needs clear eligibility, while gradual retirement should remain a practical option rather than depend entirely on individual employers' goodwill. A construction worker with documented physical limitations should not have to demonstrate the same remaining work capacity as an adviser who can reduce hours and perform lighter duties. Clear eligibility rules also make earlier access predictable for workers planning their exit, while preventing an occupational exception from becoming an arbitrary favour granted by individual managers. Pension reform should balance contribution periods with healthy life expectancy and occupational demands, rather than use longevity alone to justify a uniform retirement age.
